# HealthKit

<!-- generated:header (isim/tools/coverage-summary.py; do not edit by hand) -->
**Symbols:** 20.4% of Apple's iOS API (546 of 2672, exact) · **Rows:** 11: 6 ✅ 1 🟡 4 ❌ · **iOS:** 8.0+
<!-- /generated:header -->

**Area:** [Location, personal data & sensors](../COVERAGE.md#location) · **Apple:** [HealthKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit) · **Issues:** [`area:location`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Alocation)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** a JSON sample store (`isim/swift/overlays/HealthKit/Store.swift`) and the Health access sheet.
- **Workouts** (issue #418): workouts, their events, activities, statistics and routes are kept in the same database;
  `HKWorkoutBuilder` builds them on every iOS version, and from iOS 26 a workout session on iPhone collects a simulated
  exerciser's heart rate, energy and distance (`isim/swift/overlays/HealthKit/WorkoutBuilder.swift`).
- **Objective-C / C interface:** headers in `isim/sdk-src/Frameworks/HealthKit` over the overlay's classes; not yet
  `HKStatisticsCollectionQuery` and `dateOfBirthComponents` (isim's Foundation has no `NSDateComponents`).

| HealthKit | 🟡 | ≤17 | `isHealthDataAvailable` true on iPhone; Health Access sheet (per-type write/read switches, Turn On All) remembered per app; quantity/category samples stored in `$ISIM_DATA/Library/Health`, unit conversion, sample/statistics/statistics-collection/observer queries; read denial hidden like iOS; workouts (the rows below); characteristics unset, no clinical records. Missing: correlations, activity summaries; characteristics are fixed. Tested: test_personal |

Tested (HelloWorkout: test_workout; HelloAccessories: test_devices) |
| Workouts: `HKWorkout` (`workoutActivityType`, `duration`, `workoutEvents`, `workoutActivities`, `allStatistics`, `statistics(for:)`, the deprecated totals and initializers), `HKWorkoutEvent`, `HKWorkoutActivity`, `HKWorkoutType`, the workout predicates (`predicateForWorkouts(with:)`, by duration, by a statistic's sum, minimum, maximum or average, by activity), `predicateForWorkoutActivities(…)`, `predicateForObjects(from:)` for a workout, `HKSamplePredicate.workout`, the sort identifiers, predicate key paths and metadata keys | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted (issue #418): workouts are kept in the device's Health database with their events, activities and statistics (sums for cumulative types; average, minimum, maximum and most recent for the others), and the samples a builder added belong to the workout. The duration leaves out paused stretches. Tested (HelloWorkout: test_workout; HelloSensorsObjC) |
| `HKWorkoutBuilder` (`beginCollection`, `add(_:)`, `addWorkoutEvents`, `addMetadata`, `addWorkoutActivity`, `updateActivity`, `endCollection`, `finishWorkout`, `discardWorkout`, `elapsedTime(at:)`, `statistics(for:)`, `allStatistics`, `seriesBuilder(for:)`, the async variants) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: samples are saved as they are added (each needs its type's write permission; `beginCollection` needs permission to write workouts) and are deleted again by `discardWorkout`; `finishWorkout` saves the workout and finishes the route builders it handed out. Tested (HelloWorkout, HelloSensorsObjC) |
| Workout routes: `HKWorkoutRouteBuilder` (`insertRouteData`, `addMetadata`, `finishRoute(with:metadata:)`), `HKWorkoutRoute`, `HKSeriesBuilder`, `HKSeriesSample`, `HKSeriesType` (`workoutRoute()`, `heartbeat()`), `HKWorkoutRouteQuery` (with a date interval too), `HKWorkoutRouteQueryDescriptor`, `HKSamplePredicate.workoutRoute` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: a route keeps its locations in the database, attached to its workout; the query hands them over in batches of 100. Heartbeat series are not recorded (the type exists). Tested (HelloWorkout, HelloSensorsObjC) |
| Workout sessions: `HKWorkoutSession` (states, `prepare`, `startActivity(with:)`, `pause`, `resume`, `stopActivity(with:)`, `end`, `beginNewActivity`, `endCurrentActivity`, `currentActivity`), `HKWorkoutSessionDelegate`, `HKWorkoutSessionState`, `HKWorkoutSessionType`, `HKHealthStore.workoutSessionMirroringStartHandler` | 🟡 | 17.0 | adapted: the delegate hears each state change, the generated pause and resume events and new activities on a background queue, as on iOS; one running session at a time (another gets `errorAnotherWorkoutSessionStarted`). isim has no Apple Watch: no session is mirrored to iPhone, `sendToRemoteWorkoutSession` fails, `startWatchApp(with:)` fails. Tested (HelloWorkout on iOS 26 and 27) |
| Live workouts on iPhone (iOS 26): `HKWorkoutSession(healthStore:configuration:)`, `associatedWorkoutBuilder()`, `HKLiveWorkoutBuilder` (`dataSource`, `delegate`, `workoutSession`, `shouldCollectWorkoutEvents`, `elapsedTime`, `currentWorkoutActivity`), `HKLiveWorkoutBuilderDelegate`, `HKLiveWorkoutDataSource` (`typesToCollect`, `enableCollection(for:predicate:)`, `disableCollection(for:)`), `HKHealthStore.recoverActiveWorkoutSession` | ✅ | 26.0 | adapted: isim has no heart-rate sensor or GPS track, so the data source is a simulated exerciser for the activity: the heart rate rises from 72 toward 88–152 bpm, active energy and distance at the activity's pace (running 2.9 m/s, about 11 kcal a minute), one sample of each type a second while the session runs and the app may write that type. The samples go to the Health database like a watch's; pauses leave gaps. `recoverActiveWorkoutSession` returns the session running in the app. Tested (HelloWorkout: test_workout on iOS 26 and 27, `os_matrix`) |

The first query (no anchor) returns no deletions, as on iOS; the limit counts samples and deletions; `updateHandler` runs after each save or delete while the query runs. Tested (HelloSensors: test_sensors_and_health, every iOS version; HelloSensorsObjC: test_sensors_objc) |
